name: regexec
prose: Executes the compiled regular expression preg against string, filling pmatch with up to nmatch sub-match offsets, and returns 0 on a match or an REG_* error code. It first reads g = preg->re_g (so preg and preg->re_g must be valid) and returns REG_BADPAT if preg->re_magic is not MAGIC1 or g->magic is not MAGIC2. It then asserts that g->iflags does not have the BAD bit; in a build where asserts are enabled that aborts, and otherwise a BAD pattern makes it return REG_BADPAT. It reduces eflags with GOODFLAGS (only REG_NOTBOL, REG_NOTEOL and REG_STARTEND survive unless REDEBUG is defined). It then calls mmatcher when MB_CUR_MAX > 1, otherwise smatcher when g->nstates fits in the small state-set type (CHAR_BIT * sizeof(states1)) and REG_LARGE is not set, and otherwise lmatcher, returning that matcher's result. In those matchers (engine.c matcher), with REG_STARTEND the subject is the range string + pmatch[0].rm_so to string + pmatch[0].rm_eo (REG_INVARG if the end precedes the start), otherwise string up to its NUL; the matcher result is 0, REG_NOMATCH, REG_INVARG or REG_ESPACE as far as read here.
note: regexec.c:201-227 read in full; engine.c matcher read through line 349 only (lines 209-221 cited for STARTEND/INVARG, 295-302 for NOMATCH, 325-328 for ESPACE); the remainder of matcher not read ("partly read"). Reviewers: original (contract omits NOMATCH/BADPAT paths) right but contract removed; round 2 (REG_STARTEND uses pmatch[0] offsets, not string[0]/string[1]) right, engine.c:212-214; round 15 (assert aborts in debug builds, so BADPAT only in non-debug) right, 216-218. Tally 3 right.

name: res_nsearch
prose: Resolver search: queries name for the given class and type, applying the search list, and returns the positive response length stored in answer on success or a non-positive value (-1 in all return statements written in this function; the other returns pass on a callee's value) on failure. It clears errno, sets res_h_errno to HOST_NOT_FOUND, counts the dots and notes a trailing dot. If the name has no dots and res_hostalias finds an alias it returns res_nquery for the alias, so that result (and whatever res_h_errno it left, not necessarily NOERROR) is what the caller gets. If the dots reach statp->ndots or there is a trailing dot it first queries the name as is through res_nquerydomain; a positive result or any result when there is a trailing dot is returned directly; if errno is ECONNREFUSED it sets res_h_errno to TRY_AGAIN and returns -1; res_h_errno NO_DATA or HOST_NOT_FOUND (or TRY_AGAIN with rcode SERVFAIL) lets it go on and the code is saved, any other error returns -1 immediately. It then, if there are no dots and RES_DEFNAMES is set or there are dots, no trailing dot and RES_DNSRCH is set, loops over statp->dnsrch calling res_nquerydomain for each domain (skipping the root domain if the name was already tried as is): a positive result is returned; ECONNREFUSED gives res_h_errno TRY_AGAIN and -1; NO_DATA is counted and the search continues, as does HOST_NOT_FOUND and TRY_AGAIN with rcode SERVFAIL (counted); any other error ends the loop, and without RES_DNSRCH the loop ends after one domain. If the final res_h_errno is not NO_DATA/HOST_NOT_FOUND/(TRY_AGAIN with SERVFAIL) it goes to giveup; otherwise it tries the name as is once more unless already tried (or the root is on the list, or no dots with RES_NOTLDQUERY set after a search), returning a positive result. At giveup it sets res_h_errno to the saved as-is error if one was saved, else NO_DATA if any NO_DATA was seen, else TRY_AGAIN if a TRY_AGAIN with SERVFAIL was seen, else leaves it as the last query set it, and returns -1.
note: res_query.c:202-389 read in full; res_nquerydomain, res_hostalias, res_nquery not read. Reviewers: round 1 (success does not guarantee NOERROR, e.g. the hostalias path) right; round 2 (no zero return) right for the explicit returns here (only -1 and passed-through callee values); round 15 (ECONNREFUSED after the as-is query sets TRY_AGAIN rather than the saved error) right, 241-244. Tally 3 right.

name: send_dg
prose: Sends the query datagram buf (buflen bytes) to nameserver number ns over UDP and waits for a matching reply, which it stores in ans (anssiz bytes); the optional kqueue descriptor kq is an extra first parameter when USE_KQUEUE is defined. Return values: the reply length resplen (> 0) when an acceptable reply arrived; 1 when the reply has the TC bit set and RES_IGNTC is not set (v_circuit is set to 1 and the socket is closed, so the caller retries over TCP); -1 when a new socket cannot be created for a reason other than an unsupported protocol/family, or, in a build using select, when the new descriptor is above highestFD (res_nclose is called and errno set to ENOTSOCK before the check), in both cases with *terrno = errno; and 0 in the other failure cases: socket creation failing with EPROTONOSUPPORT, EPFNOSUPPORT or EAFNOSUPPORT (no *terrno), connect, send or sendto failing (socket closed), the timeout expiring (*gotsomewhere set to 1), select/poll/kevent failing with an error other than EINTR (socket closed), recvfrom returning <= 0 (socket closed, *gotsomewhere already set to 1), a reply shorter than HFIXEDSZ (*terrno set to EMSGSIZE, socket closed), a reply with rcode FORMERR when RES_USE_EDNS0 is set (RES_F_EDNS0ERR set in statp->_flags, socket closed), and a reply with rcode SERVFAIL, NOTIMP or REFUSED (socket closed) when statp->pfcode is 0 (if pfcode is non-zero it falls through to the TC check and then returns resplen). It creates and, unless RES_INSECURE1 is set, connects the socket on first use, computes the timeout as (retrans << tries), divided by nscount when ns > 0, at least 1 second, and loops waiting: an EINTR, a reply whose id differs from the query's, a reply from an address that is not one of our servers (unless RES_INSECURE1) or a reply whose question does not match (unless RES_INSECURE2) is ignored and waiting continues until the deadline.
note: slice cut the head; whole function at res_send.c:812-1084 was read; the part of the preamble about the debug printing macros was skipped and the helper functions (res_nclose, res_ourserver_p, res_queriesmatch) were not read. Reviewers: original (omits return 1 for truncated answer; many fatal errors return 0, not -1) right, 1068-1077 and 957-1000; round 15 (-1 with ENOTSOCK when the new fd exceeds highestFD) right for select builds, 844-849 then 850-862. Tally 2 right.

name: __rpc_get_time_offset
prose: Obtains the time difference between a remote host and the local clock: it zeroes *td, finds the server's address, asks rpcbind for its time (RPCB_GETTIME over TCP) or, if that fails, reads the port-37 time service over TCP or UDP, and stores remote minus local seconds in td->tv_sec. It returns 1 if a remote time was obtained and 0 otherwise (the 0 returns leave td zeroed). If *uaddr is NULL: if both srv and thost are non-NULL it prints a message and returns 0; without srv it builds one from thost and netid with get_server (returns 0 if that fails, and frees the endpoints it built on later failures); it picks the TCP endpoint if there is one, else the UDP endpoint, and returns 0 if there is neither; if *uaddr is non-NULL it is used as the address. It then rewrites the address to the form a1.a2.a3.a4.0.111 using sscanf on the first four fields (the sscanf result is not checked), converts it to a sockaddr (return 0 on failure), and creates a TCP client handle to rpcbind (return 0 on failure) and calls RPCBPROC_GETTIME with a 5-second timeout; success marks the time valid. Otherwise it destroys the handle, converts the address to the port-37 form and opens a socket of the chosen type (any failure there jumps to the cleanup with the time invalid), and for UDP sends a datagram and waits up to 20 seconds with select, then receives the 4-byte time; for TCP it connects with a 20-second alarm and reads 4 bytes; the value is converted with ntohl and TOFFSET is subtracted. On the cleanup path it closes any open socket, destroys any client handle, cancels the alarm and restores the old SIGALRM handler. If the time is valid it sets *uaddr to a strdup of the address used when *uaddr was NULL (the result of strdup is not checked), adds 1 to the local gettimeofday seconds when they exceed 500000 (tested on tv_sec, not on tv_usec, so this is not a rounding to the nearest second based on microseconds), stores the signed difference remote minus local in td->tv_sec with td->tv_usec 0, and returns 1; otherwise it prints "unable to get the server's time." and returns 0. Endpoints built by get_server are freed before returning when it allocated them.
note: slice cut the head; real name __rpc_get_time_offset at auth_time.c:234-497, read in full (helper functions get_server, uaddr_to_sockaddr, free_eps not read). Reviewer round 17 (rounding uses tv_sec > 500000, not tv_usec, so not rounded to the nearest second) right, 484. Tally 1 right.

name: getnetid
prose: Looks up the netid string for key in the file /etc/netid (NETIDFILE), optionally falling back to NIS, and copies the value into ret (which must be large enough for the value; it is copied with strcpy). It returns 1 when a file record whose first field equals key is found, with its value copied to ret; 2 (only when YP is defined) when a NIS lookup in the netid map succeeded, with the NIS value copied to ret; and 0 otherwise, in which case ret is not modified. If the file cannot be opened the function returns 0 without YP, and with YP it tries NIS once and returns 2 on success or 0 on failure. It reads the file line by line (1024-byte buffer): lines starting with '#' are skipped; a line starting with '+' triggers the NIS lookup (yp_get_default_domain then yp_match on key; on any NIS failure it continues with the next line) when YP is defined, and is skipped when it is not; any other line is split into a key (up to the first space or tab) and the first non-empty value token (delimiters space, tab, '#', newline); a line without a value token prints "Bad record" on stderr and is skipped, and a line whose key equals key stops the search. End of file gives 0. The file is closed before returning if it was opened, and the buffer returned by yp_match is freed after copying.
note: slice cut the head; real name getnetid (not _getnetid) at netnamer.c:236-327, read in full. The old prose is consistent with the YP build; added that '+' lines are skipped when YP is not defined and that the NIS result is 2.

name: svc_getreq_common
prose: Services pending RPC requests on the transport registered for descriptor fd (fd must be a valid index of __svc_xports); returns nothing. It sets up a local credential area, reads xprt = __svc_xports[fd] under a read lock on svc_fd_lock (the lock is dropped right after the read) and returns without doing anything if that is NULL. Otherwise it loops: if SVC_RECV yields a message it copies program, version, procedure and credentials into a local svc_req and calls _authenticate; if that returns something other than AUTH_OK it sends svcerr_auth(xprt, why) unless why is RPCSEC_GSS_NODISPATCH, in which case it sends nothing, and goes to the end-of-iteration check. Otherwise it searches the registered services (svc_head) for the program and version, calls the matching sc_dispatch(&r, xprt) and goes to the end-of-iteration check; if the program is registered with other versions only it calls svcerr_progvers with the lowest and highest registered versions, and if the program is not registered it calls svcerr_noprog. Only in the cases where SVC_RECV returned false or an error reply was sent (not after a dispatch or an auth failure) does it then take the read lock and leave the loop if __svc_xports[fd] is no longer xprt (the transport was replaced or deregistered during the call). At the end-of-iteration check it calls SVC_STAT: if the transport has died (XPRT_DIED) it calls SVC_DESTROY(xprt) and leaves; otherwise the loop repeats while SVC_STAT returned XPRT_MOREREQS. svc_fd_lock is not held at return.
note: svc.c:619-710 read in full; the cred area is a local buffer (628-632), so there is no caller precondition about it. Reviewers: original (cred_area is local; no credential freeing in the code) right; round 15 (omits the RPCSEC_GSS_NODISPATCH path where no svcerr_auth is sent) right, 662-663. Tally 2 right.

name: float64_to_int32
prose: Converts the IEEE double a to a 32-bit signed integer, rounding according to the global float_rounding_mode, and returns it. It extracts the fraction, exponent and sign; for a NaN (exponent 0x7FF with a non-zero fraction) the sign is treated as positive; a non-zero exponent adds the implicit leading bit; it shifts the significand right by 0x42C minus the exponent with sticky-bit jamming when that count is positive and leaves it unshifted otherwise, and hands the result to roundAndPackInt32. That function rounds with nearest-even, toward zero, toward negative infinity or toward positive infinity according to float_rounding_mode, sets float_flag_inexact in float_exception_flags when any discarded bits were non-zero, and, when the rounded magnitude does not fit in 32 bits or its sign no longer matches, sets float_flag_invalid and returns 0x7FFFFFFF for a positive (or NaN) input or 0x80000000 for a negative input; an infinity or a NaN therefore gives 0x7FFFFFFF or 0x80000000 with float_flag_invalid. The value -2^31 is returned without the invalid flag.
note: slice cut the head; real function float64_to_int32 at softfloat.c:2330-2345 with roundAndPackInt32 at 111-147, both read in full. Reviewer round 15 (the code truncates toward zero and does not honour float_rounding_mode) is wrong: roundAndPackInt32 reads float_rounding_mode at line 118 and picks the increment accordingly (119-134); the truncating function is float64_to_int32_round_to_zero, a different function. Tally 1 wrong.

name: stdc_first_trailing_zero_ul
prose: Takes an unsigned long x and returns an unsigned int: 0 if every bit of x is one (x == ~0UL), otherwise 1 plus the index (counted from 0 at the least significant bit) of the least significant zero bit of x, computed as __builtin_ctzl(~x) + 1; the result therefore lies between 1 and the width of unsigned long when x is not all ones. It reads no memory other than its argument and has no side effects.
note: stdc_first_trailing_zero.c:25-53 region read (this function is the third of four width variants). Previous contract left out: the earlier versions hard-code the 64-bit width or use a builtin Frama-C does not know, and were rejected; an ACSL contract that does not depend on the width was not written. Reviewers: round 2 (hard-coded 64-bit ULONG_MAX) right, the code uses ~0UL.

name: stdc_trailing_ones_ui
prose: Takes an unsigned int x and returns the number of consecutive one bits starting at the least significant bit. If x == ~0U it returns UINT_WIDTH; otherwise it returns __builtin_ctz(~x), the index of the lowest zero bit of x, so the low result bits of x are one and the next bit is zero. It reads no memory other than its argument and has no side effects.
note: stdc_trailing_ones.c:30-36 read. Reviewers: round 1 (the contract shifts by the width in the all-ones case) right, round 15 (contract hard-codes 32 and 4294967295 rather than UINT_WIDTH/~0U) right; contract removed rather than rewritten.

name: stdc_trailing_ones_ul
prose: Takes an unsigned long x and returns the number of consecutive one bits starting at the least significant bit. If x == ~0UL it returns ULONG_WIDTH; otherwise it returns __builtin_ctzl(~x), the index of the lowest zero bit of x, so the low result bits of x are one and the next bit is zero. It reads no memory other than its argument and has no side effects.
note: stdc_trailing_ones.c:38-44 read. Reviewers: round 1 (shift by the width in the all-ones case) right; round 15 (hard-coded 64 and 18446744073709551615 rather than ULONG_WIDTH/~0UL) right; contract removed.

name: stdc_trailing_ones_ull
prose: Takes an unsigned long long x and returns the number of consecutive one bits starting at the least significant bit. If x == ~0ULL it returns ULLONG_WIDTH; otherwise it returns __builtin_ctzll(~x), the index of the lowest zero bit of x, so the low result bits of x are one and the next bit is zero. It reads no memory other than its argument and has no side effects.
note: stdc_trailing_ones.c:46-52 read. Reviewers: round 1 (shift by the width in the all-ones case) right; round 15 (hard-coded 64 and 18446744073709551615 rather than ULLONG_WIDTH/~0ULL) right; contract removed.

name: _fseeko
prose: Repositions stream fp to offset relative to whence (SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR or SEEK_END) and returns 0 on success or -1 with errno set; ltest, when non-zero, additionally requires the resulting position to fit in a long. Early failures return -1 before touching the stream: ESPIPE if the stream has no seek function; for SEEK_CUR a failing _ftello (its errno is left as is), ESPIPE if the current offset is negative, EOVERFLOW if adding offset would exceed OFF_MAX or (with ltest) exceed LONG_MAX, EINVAL if the sum is negative; EINVAL for a negative SEEK_SET offset or an unknown whence. It then allocates a buffer if none exists and chooses between an optimised path and a "dumb" path (flush, then seek to the requested place). The optimised path is used only for a read-only seekable regular-file stream (otherwise it sets __SNPT and, when first examining the stream, may set __SOPT and the block size) and computes the target for SEEK_END from fstat (EOVERFLOW or EINVAL for an out-of-range target, ltest respected); if the target is inside the current buffer it just moves the read pointer, frees any ungetc pushback, clears __SEOF and resets the multibyte state and returns 0; otherwise it seeks to the block boundary below the target, refills, and positions inside the buffer, also clearing pushback, __SEOF and the conversion state; any seek, refill or short-read problem falls to the dumb path. The dumb path calls __sflush and _sseek (returning -1 with errno from those calls if either fails), fails with EOVERFLOW and sets __SERR when ltest is set and the new position exceeds LONG_MAX, and otherwise frees pushback, empties the buffer, clears __SEOF, resets the multibyte state and returns 0. On failure the stream may already have been altered (flags set, buffer allocated, file offset changed), and errno can come from _ftello, _fstat, __srefill, __sflush or _sseek as well as ESPIPE, EINVAL and EOVERFLOW.
note: fseek.c:90-297 read in full (comments skipped), HASUB/FREEUB macros and callee bodies not read. Reviewers: original (stream may already be modified on failure) right, e.g. 173, 176-177, 284; round 15 (errno also from _ftello/_fstat/__srefill/_sseek failures) right, 118-119, 280-282. Tally 2 right.

name: _gettemp
prose: Fills in the trailing X characters of the template path (excluding the last slen characters, a suffix) with random characters from padchar and tries to create or check the resulting name, returning 1 on success and 0 on failure with errno set by the failing step. It returns 0 with errno EINVAL if doopen is non-NULL and domkdir is set together, if slen is negative, if oflags has bits other than O_APPEND, O_DIRECT, O_SHLOCK, O_EXLOCK, O_SYNC, O_CLOEXEC and O_CLOFORK, or if the suffix would start at or before the start of path (slen not smaller than strlen(path)) or contains a '/'; ENAMETOOLONG if strlen(path) is MAXPATHLEN or more. It replaces each trailing 'X' before the suffix with arc4random_uniform characters of padchar, then loops: with doopen set it opens the name with _openat(dfd, ..., oflags | O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_RDWR, 0600), storing the descriptor in *doopen and returning 1 on success or 0 on an error other than EEXIST; with domkdir it does mkdir(path, 0700) with the same rule; otherwise it calls lstat and returns whether errno was ENOENT (1 if the name does not exist, 0 for another lstat error; when the name exists it continues). On a collision it saves the initial random characters and increments the characters like an odometer through padchar, returning 0 when every combination has been tried, in which case errno is whatever the last call left (EEXIST after open or mkdir collisions, but not set by this code after a successful lstat), and returning 0 with errno EIO if a template character is not found in padchar.
note: mktemp.c:113-197 read in full (comments skipped). Reviewers: original (on collision exhaustion after lstat success it returns 0 without setting errno) right, 163-164 and 175-176; round 15 (slen must be smaller than strlen(path), EINVAL otherwise) right, 134-140. Tally 2 right.

name: __srefill
prose: Refills the read buffer of stream fp and returns 0 on success or EOF; the caller is expected to hold fp's lock (the function does not lock fp itself, and its flush of fp itself at the line-buffered step is done without locking). It initialises stdio if needed, and ORIENT(fp, -1) only sets the stream orientation to byte if it was unset; it does not fail on a wide-oriented stream and the function does not set EINVAL. It then sets fp->_r to 0 and returns EOF at once if __SEOF is set. If the stream is not in read mode: when it is also not read/write it sets errno to EBADF and __SERR and returns EOF; when it was writing it calls __sflush (returning EOF if that fails), switches it to reading and sets __SRD. If it was already reading and has an ungetc buffer it frees it and, if the saved count _ur is non-zero, restores the read pointer and returns 0 without reading. It allocates a buffer if none exists. For a line-buffered or unbuffered stream it sets __SIGN on fp, calls _fwalk(lflush) to flush line-buffered writers, clears __SIGN, and flushes fp itself with __sflush only if fp is line-buffered and in write mode (the result of that flush is ignored). It then reads up to the buffer size with _sread into the buffer and clears __SMOD (not cleared on the earlier returns). If the read returns 0 it sets __SEOF and returns EOF; if it returns a negative value it sets _r to 0 and __SERR and returns EOF; otherwise it returns 0 with _r holding the byte count.
note: refill.c:44-142 read (comments partly skipped); ORIENT in local.h:143-146. Reviewers: round 1 (the caller must hold fp's lock; this stream is flushed without locking) right; round 2 (__SMOD not cleared on the early returns or the ungetc return) right, 131; round 15 (no EINVAL for a wide-oriented stream, no _r = 0 before; the flush of this stream only for line-buffered writers) right, 71-73 and 126-127. Tally 3 right.

name: __wcsconv
prose: Converts the wide string wcsarg to a newly malloc'd multibyte string for printf's %ls, limited to prec bytes when prec >= 0 (no limit when prec < 0), and returns it NUL-terminated, or NULL on failure; the caller must free it. With prec < 0 the whole string (up to its terminating NUL) is measured with wcsrtombs; NULL is returned if that fails on an unconvertible character. With 0 <= prec < 128 the buffer size is simply prec bytes without examining the string. With prec >= 128 it counts bytes with wcrtomb from the start, stopping at a NUL wide character, at a conversion error, or at the first character that would take the byte count over prec; that loop reads wide characters up to and including the one at which it stops, so a string without a NUL needs at least one readable wide character beyond the converted prefix. It allocates nbytes + 1 bytes (NULL if malloc fails), then converts with wcsrtombs into that buffer limited to nbytes bytes; if that returns -1 (for prec < 128 this can happen on an unconvertible character within the limit) it frees the buffer and returns NULL; otherwise it NUL-terminates the converted bytes and returns them. For prec >= 128, an unconvertible character found by the counting loop ends the count there, so the result is the truncated prefix before it, not NULL.
note: vfprintf.c:212-262 read in full (slice began mid-file). Reviewers: round 1 (prec >= 128: invalid wide char within precision gives a truncated non-NULL result) right in that the counting loop stops before it, 242-246; round 2 (0 <= prec < 128: wcsrtombs can fail and return NULL) right, 255-259; round 15 (precondition too weak: the scan reads one extra wide character) right, 241-244. Whether wcsrtombs stops without examining the next character once the destination length is reached was not checked in the libc source (assumed from standard behaviour). Tally 3 right.

name: __svfscanf
prose: Core of scanf for a stream: parses the format fmt0 and reads input from fp (using the locale for wide and floating conversions), storing converted values through pointers fetched from ap, and returns an int count or EOF. It sets the stream orientation to byte if unset. For each format character: end of format returns nassigned; white space in the format skips input white space; an ordinary character (or "%%") must equal the next input byte, otherwise it takes the match_failure exit (input_failure exit if no input can be read). After '%', flags and sizes are parsed (the flags '*' suppress assignment; h, hh, l, ll, j, q, t, z, L; a decimal width; %w<8|16|32|64> with an optional f, any other w width goes to match_failure); a trailing '%' at the end of the format returns EOF at once; an unknown conversion character takes match_failure; %n stores the characters consumed so far (unless suppressed) and does not count as a conversion. The conversions are %d %i %o %u %x %X %b %B %p (read with parseint then strtoimax_l or strtoumax_l and stored by the size flag), %a %A %e %E %f %F %g %G (parsefloat then strtof_l, strtod_l or strtold_l), %s %S, %c %C and %[ (via convert_string, convert_char, convert_ccl and the wide variants). Input white space is skipped before a conversion unless it is %c or %[; hitting end of input at that point or during a conversion that reports a negative count takes input_failure; a parseint or parsefloat count of 0 and an empty %[ match take match_failure. Each completed conversion adds to nconversions and, unless suppressed, nassigned. At input_failure it returns nassigned if at least one conversion was completed and EOF otherwise; at match_failure it returns nassigned (which may be 0, not EOF).
note: slice cut the head and tail; the real function is __svfscanf at vfscanf.c:482-864 (vfscanf is a weak reference to __vfscanf which calls it), read in full except the converter helpers (convert_*, parseint, parsefloat, __sccl) which were not read ("partly read": callee bodies). Reviewer round 17 (match failure with zero assignments returns EOF) is wrong: match_failure returns nassigned at line 863; EOF only comes from input_failure with no conversions (861) or the trailing-'%' return (708). Tally 1 wrong.

name: __printf_render_float
prose: Renders one floating-point conversion to the output sink io according to pi and returns the sum of the values returned by the __printf_pad and __printf_puts calls it makes (the characters it asked to be written, as reported by those helpers). The value is taken from arg[0] as a double, or as a long double when pi->is_long_double. For %a/%A it uses __hdtoa/__hldtoa hexadecimal digits with a 0x or 0X prefix (dropped for inf/nan), with p/P exponent; for %e/%E, %f/%F and %g/%G it uses dtoa or __ldtoa (default precision DEFPREC when none is given, 1 for %g with precision 0); any other spec value fails the assert(pi->spec == 'f') (in a build with asserts) and otherwise falls to the %f path. The sign is '-' for a negative value, else pi->showsign. A value whose exponent is INT_MAX (infinity or NaN) is printed as inf/nan, or INF/NAN for an upper-case spec, with no sign for NaN. For %g it chooses between fixed and exponent form from the exponent and precision. Output order is: left padding unless zero padding or left justification applies, the sign, the 0x/0X prefix, zero padding up to the width when pi->pad is '0' and not left-justified, then the digits (in fixed form with leading "0.", digit grouping using the locale's thousands separator when pi->alt is set and the locale has grouping, the decimal point from the locale, trailing zero padding; in exponent form the digit, decimal point, remaining digits, zero padding and the exponent string), and finally right padding when pi->left is set. It then calls __printf_flush(io), frees the dtoa buffer if it is non-NULL, and returns the accumulated count.
note: slice cut the head; real name __printf_render_float at xprintf_float.c:148-422 (not printfloat), read in full except helper bodies (exponent, PRINTANDPAD, __printf_pad, __hdtoa). Reviewer round 17 (grouping is controlled by the ' flag pi->group, not the alt flag) is wrong: grouping is set from pi->alt at lines 187-188 (no use of pi->group in the function). Tally 1 wrong.

name: __merge_environ
prose: Re-synchronises the library's internal environment table with the program's environ array when the program has replaced or emptied environ, returning 0 or -1. It does nothing and returns 0 if intEnviron is NULL (no internal copy exists), or if environ equals intEnviron and not (envActive > 0 and environ[0] == NULL). Otherwise, if envActive > 0 it sets origEnviron to NULL and calls __clean_env(false), which deactivates all internal variables, resets envActive to 0 and removes putenv entries; since origEnviron is NULL at that point, __clean_env does not restore or free intEnviron. It then sets origEnviron = environ and, if environ is not NULL, walks its entries: an entry without '=' prints a warning, sets errno to EFAULT and returns -1; each other entry is inserted with __setenv(name, namelen, value, 1) and a -1 return from __setenv is returned as -1 (errno as set by __setenv). name: __libc_system
prose: Implements system(3): runs command with /bin/sh -c and returns the wait status of the child, or -1. If command is NULL it only tests whether _PATH_BSHELL is executable by the caller (eaccess with X_OK) and returns 1 if so and 0 otherwise, without forking or touching signals. Otherwise, with a spin lock held when the process is threaded, it counts concurrent callers; the first caller sets SIGINT and SIGQUIT to ignore (saving the old actions in static variables), and every caller blocks SIGCHLD, remembering the previous mask. It then forks. If fork fails it saves errno and the return value stays -1. In the child it restores the saved SIGINT/SIGQUIT actions and the saved signal mask and calls _execve on the shell, calling _exit(127) if the exec fails, so a failed exec is seen by the parent as an exit status of 127 inside the wait status. In the parent it calls _wait4 for the child, retrying on EINTR; any other wait4 error saves errno and leaves the return value -1, otherwise the return value is the wait status. Afterwards, under the lock, the last of the concurrent callers restores the saved SIGINT and SIGQUIT actions (an earlier finisher leaves them ignored), and a caller unblocks SIGCHLD only if SIGCHLD was not blocked in the mask it saw when it started. If a fork or wait4 error was saved it sets errno to it before returning the status.
note: system.c:56-137 read in full (comments skipped). Reviewers: original (NULL returns eaccess == 0 as a boolean; exec failure shows up as the wait status; -1 on fork/wait failure) right, 68-69, 106-107, 94-95, 112-117; round 15 (SIGINT/SIGQUIT are restored only by the last concurrent instance; SIGCHLD restore not guaranteed under concurrency) right, 126-131. Tally 2 right.

name: run_tests
prose: Runs one group-database (getgr*) test selected by method, optionally against a snapshot file, and returns 0 on success or -1 on failure (the rv of the DO_*_TEST macros and the snapshot write are passed through). It initialises two test data sets td and td_snap. If snapshot_file is non-NULL: when access(W_OK | R_OK) fails with ENOENT it forces method = TEST_BUILD_SNAPSHOT; when it fails with another error it prints a message and goes to the cleanup with rv = -1; when it succeeds and method is TEST_BUILD_SNAPSHOT it goes to the cleanup with rv = 0 without building anything; otherwise it reads the snapshot into td_snap. It then fills td with the system's groups through group_fill_test_data; if that returns -1 it returns -1 immediately, without destroying td or td_snap. Otherwise it switches on method: getgrnam, getgrgid or getgrent tests run against td (no snapshot) or td_snap (snapshot; getgrent compares td with td_snap in a two-pass test); the 2-pass and the two interleaved variants fill a third data set (destroyed afterwards) and compare it with td; TEST_BUILD_SNAPSHOT with a non-NULL snapshot_file writes td to the file with sdump_group; with a NULL snapshot_file it does nothing and rv is the value from group_fill_test_data (0 on success); an unknown method gives 0. At the cleanup td_snap and td are destroyed and rv is returned; that cleanup is reached on every path except the immediate return after a failed group_fill_test_data.
note: getgr_test.c:404-500 read in full; group_fill_test_data (292-313, returns 0 at its end or -1) read; the DO_*_TEST and snapshot macros not read. name: ATF_TC_BODY(sig2str_heap_after_end, tc)
prose: Generated function sig2str_heap_after_end_body(tc), the body of an ATF fortify test case; it returns nothing. It forks (requiring a non-negative result). The child disables core dumps (disable_coredumps), mallocs a buffer of SIG2STR_MAX - 1 bytes, calls sig2str(1, buf) and, if that call returns, _exit(EX_SOFTWARE), which means the fortified call did not abort. The parent waits for the child with waitpid, requiring errno to be EINTR for each wait that returns something other than the child. If the child did not die from a signal it fails the test: with "FORTIFY_SOURCE failed to abort" for exit status EX_SOFTWARE, with "setrlimit(2) failed" for EX_OSERR, and with an unexpected-status message for any other status. If the child was killed by a signal it requires that signal to be SIGABRT.
note: fortify_signal_test.c:259-308 read in full. Previous prose accurate; the child's buffer is not freed (it exits).
